priorStatuses.title: Remove the message listener during cleanup

findings.title: [P1] Restore socket-listener removal in the disposer
findings.body: After any caller invokes the returned cleanup function, the socket still retains and invokes `handler`. Repeated attach/dispose cycles accumulate listeners and captured state, causing duplicate processing, memory growth, and eventual `MaxListenersExceededWarning`.

findings.title: [P1] Clear the polling interval during cleanup
findings.body: Invoking the returned cleanup function leaves the interval active. The callback and captured state remain retained and execute every second indefinitely; repeated start/cleanup cycles stack timers, and in Node.js even one referenced interval can prevent process shutdown.

findings.title: [P1] Remove the message listener during cleanup
findings.body: This previously reported defect remains open after current-source revalidation. Evidence: Current src/socket.ts line 3 still returns an empty disposer immediately after registering handler with socket.on; the full PR diff shows this PR removed socket.off("message", handler). Invoking cleanup therefore leaves the listener registered, so repeated attach/dispose cycles retain handlers and duplicate message processing.
